content:
# Analysis

Looking at the `prod/app.yaml` Deployment:

**`spec.selector.matchLabels`:**
```yaml
app: myapp
env: prod
version: v2
```

**`spec.template.metadata.labels`:**
```yaml
app: myapp
env: prod
```

**The missing label: `version: v2`**

The selector requires the pod template to have three labels, but the template only provides two. The `dev/app.yaml` Deployment doesn't have this problem because its selector only requires `app` and `env`, which match what's in the template.

# Solution

Add `version: v2` to the pod template labels so every label in the selector is satisfied by the template. The Service's selector (`app` and `env`) will remain a subset of the template labels, so it will still correctly select the pods.

---

`prod/app.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: myapp-prod
  namespace: app
  annotations:
    eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: "<REPLACE_WITH_myapp-prod-service-role_ARN_AFTER_CREATE>"
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: myapp-prod
  namespace: app
  labels:
    app: myapp
    env: prod
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: myapp
      env: prod
      version: v2
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: myapp
        env: prod
        version: v2
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: myapp-prod
      containers:
        - name: myapp
          image: docker.io/myapp/myapp:latest
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 100m
              memory: 128Mi
            limits:
              cpu: 500m
              memory: 256Mi
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: myapp-prod
  namespace: app
spec:
  selector:
    app: myapp
    env: prod
  ports:
    - port: 80
      targetPort: 8080
  type: ClusterIP
```
